Misc. Criminal Case No. 44632 of 2025

Vinay Dohre
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Shri Ashfaq Khan - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Vps Tomar - Panel Lawyer for the State.
Shri Ashish Singh Jadoun - Advocate for the complainant.

Order 
The present application, filed under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. (corresponding to Section 483 of the BNSS, 2023), is the first one seeking grant of bail.

The applicant has been in custody since 27.08.2025 in connection with Crime No.333/2023 registered at Police Station Bhander, District Datia (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2) of IPC and Sections 5L/6 of the POSCO Act.
Kidnapping, rape and the offence under the POCSO Act is alleged against the applicant in respect of minor prosecutrix who is below 18 years.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits before this Court that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The allegations levelled against him are baseless and do not stand scrutiny in view of the surrounding circumstances.
The applicant and the prosecutrix entered into marriage of their own free will, and out of this wedlock, the prosecutrix has given birth to a child of the applicant.

At present, the prosecutrix is residing in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24431 2 MCRC-44632-2025 applicant's household with her full consent, which fact significantly undermines the veracity of the allegations made against the applicant.

The applicant is a permanent resident of District Datia, and therefore, there is no likelihood of his Vinay Dohre vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102856327/
1 tampering with evidence or influencing witnesses if released on bail.

sentences.text: The trial is likely to take considerable time for its conclusion.
The applicant undertakes to strictly abide by any conditions that this Court may deem fit to impose while granting bail.
In view of the foregoing, a prayer has been made for the grant of regular bail.

Per contra , learned Public Prosecutor/Panel Lawyer for the State as well as the counsel for the complainant has opposed the application and prayed for its rejection looking to the gravity of offence.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, coupled with the fact that the trial is likely to take considerable time for its conclusion, and bearing in mind that prolonged pre-trial incarceration militates against the fundamental right to personal liberty, and further, there being no material to indicate any likelihood of the applicant absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence, this Court finds it fit and proper to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant.

Accordingly,
without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court for his appearance on the dates given by the concerned Court, subject to compliance of the following conditions by the applicant:-
1.
The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
Certified copy as per rules.

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE pwn*
